The result includes 'reaction_id' maybe that's the template ID? Usually template_id is integer. The description says template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). In search results, each dict likely includes 'reaction_id' as the template ID. So template_id = 1914386.

We need to return mapped_rxn associated with the template that reproduces the reaction. The mapped_rxn is given in the result: '[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19].O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])[CH2:6][CH2:7][c:8]1[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]1>>[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

We should verify that this reaction indeed maps target product (our molecule) as product. The product SMILES matches target? Target: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. The product SMILES in result: [CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19] . That seems same: methyl ester (CH3O-C(=O)-) attached to a cyclopropene? Actually C5 is part of ring with double bond to C14=C15 and SiMe3. Yes matches.
